CLMA No. 12437/2017 (Delay Condonation Application in Time Barred in SPA) 
In 
SPA No. 770 of 2017 
Hon’ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
Hon’ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Mr. A.K. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel for 
the State of Uttarakhand/appellants. 
Despite the matter being listed for the caption 
of the order neither Shri Hem Chandra Joshi, 
learned counsel for the respondents present in the 
Court nor is there any representation on his behalf. 
The delay in preferring the appeal is 
condoned for the reasons stated in the affidavit 
accompanying the said application. In the orders 
under appeal the learned Single Judge had directed 
the services of the petitioners be regularize in terms 
of the 2013 Labour Regularization Rules. The 
validity of the said Rules was subjected to challenge 
in WPSB No. 616 of 2018. 
Admit. 
Post along with WPSB No. 616 of 2018. 
There shall be interim stay of the operation of 
the impugned judgment. 
 
(N.S. Dhanik, J.)                            (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MS. RITU BAHRI
AND
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
22ND FEBRUARY, 2024
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 616 OF 2018
Narendra Singh and another. 
…Petitioners
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. 
…Respondents
With
SPECIAL APPEAL No. 561 OF 2017
State of Uttarakhand and others. 
…Appellants

…Respondents
With

State of Uttarakhand and others. 
…Appellants

…Respondents
With
SPECIAL APPEAL No. 772 OF 2017
State of Uttarakhand and others. 
…Appellants
Versus
Manoj Kumar and others. 
…Respondents 2
With 
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 604 OF 2021
Dr. Spresh Bhatt. 
…Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. 
…Respondents
Counsel for the petitioners in 
WPSB No. 616/2018.
 
: Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel.
Counsel for the petitioner in WPSB 
No. 604/2021.
: Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, learned counsel. 
Counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
: Mr. J.P. Joshi, learned Additional 
Advocate General for the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
Counsel for respondents in SPA 
Nos. 561/2017, 770/2017 and 
772/2017.
: Mr. Hem Chandra Joshi, learned 
counsel.
Counsel for the intervener in WPSB 
No. 616/2018.
: Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel.
Counsel for respondent nos. 10 & 
11 in WPSB No. 616/2018.
: Mr. D.S. Patni, learned counsel. 
Counsel for Kumaun University. : Mr. B.D. Upadhyaya, learned Senior 
Counsel assisted by Ms. Mamta Bisht, 
learned counsel. 
JUDGMENT : (per Ms. Ritu Bahri, C.J.)
This order shall dispose of above mentioned 
05 cases, as common questions of facts and law are
involved in them.
2. The short question for consideration in these 
cases is that, after making the Rules of Regularization in 
the year 2011, the State of Uttarakhand had regularized 
all those employees, who had completed 10 years of 
service. However, subsequently, Rules were made on 
31.12.2013 for regularizing those employees, who were  3
not covered as per the Rules of 2011, and these Rules
were made, keeping in view the fact that the State of 
Uttarakhand came into being on 09.11.2000, and many 
departments came into being after 2000, and there were 
number of employees, who could not complete 10 years 
of service, when 2011 Rules were framed, and they 
could not be regularized. Being a beneficial legislation, 
the State of Uttarakhand came up with the Rules of 
2013, and reduced the period of regularization from 10 
years to 05 years.
3. The grievance of the petitioners in this batch 
of cases is that the period of 10 years could not have 
been reduced to 05 years. 
4. Since the present case is a special case, where 
the State was not in existence before 2000, 10 years’
period could not be completed by number of employees, 
as per the 2011 Rules, once the State came into being 
on 09.11.2000. Hence, in order to accommodate those 
employees, this Policy of 31.12.2013 was made. The 
grievance of the petitioners is only that, by creating the 
Rules of 2013, the State of Uttarakhand has reduced the 
period to 05 years, rather than restricting it to 10 years.  4
5. Even if this argument of counsel for the 
petitioners is taken into consideration today, number of 
employees, who have been regularized after giving 05 
years of service, have now served for almost 11 more 
years after 2013, and even if this condition of 05 years 
is to be amended, the services of those employees, who 
have already been regularized as per the 2013 Rules,
cannot be de-regularized, as they have served for 
almost 14 years now. 
6. In the present case, there was an interim 
order of stay dated 04.12.2018, that no orders of 
regularization will be passed by the State Government,
under the 2013 Rules. Hence, since 04.12.2018 no 
regularization orders have been passed. All those 
persons, who have been regularized as per the 2013 
Rules before 04.12.2018, have worked for more than 
13-14 years now. With respect to other candidates, who 
have to be regularized now, they can be regularized, as 
per the 2013 Rules, by taking into consideration 10 
years’ service, instead of 05 years, as of now. 
7. Accordingly, the 2013 Rules are being 
modified that, after 04.12.2018, 10 years’ period will be 
taken into consideration for regularization.  5
8. In view of the above, all the above mentioned 
Writ Petitions/ Special Appeals are disposed of. 
9. Pending application(s), if any, also stand 
disposed of accordingly. 
______________
RITU BAHRI, C.J.
___________________
ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Dt: 22nd February, 2024
Rahul

State of Uttarakhand & others ...........Appellants
Vs.
Naresh Kumar & others .........Respondents
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, learned Additional Advocate 
General for the State- appellants.
2. Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal and Mr. Hem Chandra 
Joshi, learned counsel for the respondents.
Delay Condonation App. in Review App. (12439 of 2025)
3. As per office report, there is delay of 635 days in 
filing Review Application (MCC No.12440 of 2025).
4. Objection to delay condonation application is filed by 
the respondents. However, for reasons indicated in the 
affidavit filed in support of review application, we are 
inclined to condone the delay. Accordingly, delay 
condonation application is allowed and delay is condoned.
Review Application (MCC No.12440 of 2025) 
5. Heard on review application.
6. Learned State Counsel submits that this appeal was 
wrongly connected with writ petition filed by Narendra 
Singh & another [Writ Petition (S/B) No.616 of 2018] and 
was decided by a common judgment dated 22.02.2024, 
although, the issue involved in this appeal was entirely 
different from the issues raised in Writ Petition (S/B) 
No.616 of 2018.
7. It is contended that in Writ Petition (S/B) No.616 of 
2018, validity of Rules framed by State of Uttarakhand for 
regularization of ad hoc, contract or part-time employees 
was challenged on the ground that as per law declared by 
Hon’ble Supreme Court in State of Karnataka & others  vs. Uma Devi & others, reported in 2006 (4) SCC 1, no 
one can be regularized in service before completing 
minimum period of ten years, while the Regularization 
Rules, 2013 provide for regularization of those who have 
completed five years of service. In Writ Petition (S/B) 
No.616 of 2018, this Court held as follows:-
“6. In the present case, there was an interim order of stay dated 
04.12.2018, that no orders of regularization will be passed by the 
State Government, under the 2013 Rules. Hence, since 
04.12.2018 no regularization orders have been passed. All those 
persons, who have been regularized as per the 2013 Rules before 
04.12.2018, have worked for more than 13-14 years now. With 
respect to other candidates, who have to be regularized now, they 
can be regularized, as per the 2013 Rules, by taking into 
consideration 10 years’ service, instead of 05 years, as of now.
7. Accordingly, the 2013 Rules are being modified that, after 
04.12.2018, 10 years’ period will be taken into consideration for 
regularization.”
8. Learned State Counsel submits that State has filed 
this special appeal challenging judgment rendered by 
learned Single Judge in different writ petitions, whereby 
State Authorities were directed to regularize writ petitioners 
in those cases under Regularization Rules, 2013. He 
submits that since this Court, in the judgment dated 
22.02.2024, rendered in Writ Petition (S/B) No.616 of 
2018, held that period of five years prescribed in 
Regularization Rules, 2013 shall be read as ten years, 
therefore, the issue raised in the present special appeal 
could not have been decided together with Writ Petition 
(S/B) No.616 of 2018.
9. We find substance in the contention raised by learned 
State Counsel- review applicant. Since in the judgment 
impugned in this intra-court appeal, there is a direction 
issued to State Authorities to regularize writ petitioners by 
applying Regularization Rules, 2013, while in Writ Petition 
(S/B) No.2013, this Court had held that five years’ period 
prescribed in Regularization Rules, 2013 to be read as ten 
years, therefore, this appeal was wrongly decided with Writ 
Petition (S/B) No.616 of 2018.
10. We, accordingly, review the judgment dated 
22.02.2024 qua Special Appeal No.770 of 2017 and restore  this special appeal to its original number.
11. List on 17.11.2026 for hearing on merits.
12. Review application (MCC No.12440 of 2025) stands 
disposed of.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.)
 27.10.2026 27.10.2026
NISHANT
